Subject: Post-demo recap + initial data/request items

Hi Jordan + Alicia,

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the candid discussion about Acme's support agent workflow and the throughput targets you shared. Quick recap and items I promised: 

1) What we saw today
- Demo focused on multi-turn support automation + triage classification.
- Peak concurrent sessions target: ~1,200 active chats; target median latency < 300ms for assistant responses.
- Hard constraint: store customer transcripts for 90 days; data residency in US.

2) Immediate asks from our side
- Send the sample transcript set (anonymized) you mentioned so we can run the same prompt set against shortlisted models.
- Confirm spike days (dates) so we can simulate peak batching.

3) Next steps (proposed)
- I'll share a recommended 3-model shortlist with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs + prompt set and benchmark links by Friday.
- If that looks good, we can spin up a 2-week evaluation on Redwood Dedicated with pre-seeded prompt tests and shared dashboards.

Attachments: acme_benchmarks_20261028.pdf (pdf summary), prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), redwood_model_profiles.csv (performance profiles)

Thanks — I'll follow up with the shortlist and rationale shortly.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hey Marissa — thanks for the recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Our 1,200 active chats number is concurrent during peak by region (US-east primarily). Is the benchmarking you're proposing regionalized or single-region?
- For the transcript set: we can share the anonymized CSV by EOD Monday. Will that be enough to get representative evals?

Also, curious if you can call out any obvious risks around quality regressions when we quantize models — we have a procurement preference for lower-cost inference but don't want to introduce customer-visible regressions.

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + initial data/request items

Jordan — great questions. Short answers up front, then the recommended shortlist with rationale below.

- Benchmarking region: we can run region-specific evals (US-East) and include cross-region fallbacks in the routing policy. We'll include latency percentiles per-region in the report.
- Sample transcript CSV is perfect for an initial eval. We'll run the provided prompt set against each candidate and a small holdout set for quality regression checks.
- Quantization risks: 8-bit quantization (e.g., Q8) typically preserves top-line generation quality for conversational flows, but you can see small regressions on rare token choices or long-context coherence. We recommend gating quantized variants behind quality tests (prompt set + holdout) and having automatic rollback/fallback to a float (FP16) variant for any regression above a threshold (we propose >2% drop in answer accuracy/F1).

Recommended 3-model shortlist (initial):
1) RedForm-XL (FP16, 27B) — Best quality/latency balance
   - Rationale: Strong multi-turn coherence on our prompt set; median latency ~230ms (US-East, p95 ~420ms) at 1,200 concurrent sessions with continuous batching on Dedicated. Higher vCPU & GPU memory needs; estimated cost ~ $1,350 / 1M tokens (hosted baseline).
\2) OpenLlama-30B-q8 (quantized) — Cost-optimized with acceptable quality
   - Rationale: Q8 quantized 30B shows ~10–12% lower token cost vs FP16 variants and median latency ~270ms (p95 ~520ms). We observed ~1.5% drop in top-1 accuracy on classification tasks in your prompt set — within typical tolerance, but requires regression gating. Estimated cost ~ $1,150 / 1M tokens.
\3) Redwood-Turbo-13B (mixed-precision) — Low-cost, low-latency baseline
   - Rationale: Excellent latency (median ~140ms, p95 ~280ms), cost-efficient (~$600 / 1M tokens). Quality tradeoff vs RedForm-XL is noticeable on long coherent threads and complex summarization; we recommend this for latency-sensitive flows (triage + routing) and RedForm-XL for final answer generation.
\Links & artifacts:
- Benchmarks + detailed measurement per model: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/acme/benchmarks-20261028
- Prompt set + expected outputs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/acme/prompt-sets/acme_v1.jsonl
- Eval dashboard (will be provisioned if you approve the trial): HubSpot deal RWI-2026-00123 -> link: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/RWI-2026-00123
\Proposed next steps:
- You: share anonymized transcript CSV by 2026-11-02.
- Us: run the prompt set across the 3 shortlisted variants (region-specific) and return a quality/cost/latency matrix + regression report (3 business days after data).
- If results look good: spin a 2-week Dedicated eval with dashboards and automated regression alerts; set up a mutual action plan and procurement touchpoint.
\Attachments: acme_benchmarks_20261028.pdf, prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl
\Would you like us to include a quantized fallback policy and automatic rollback in the eval? We can enable that by default.
\Best,
Marissa
